thread:
customer-alex: Hey, after rotating our API key yesterday our backend started getting 401 invalid_api_key responses from the Redwood hosted endpoint. Dashboard shows the new key active. We call it from our Node service which goes through corp-proxy.

customer-alex: Minimal curl we run from the service host (redacted key):
```bash
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Api-Key sk_live_XXXXREDACTEDXXXX' https://api.redwoodinference.example/v1/generate
``` 
response: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized\n{\"error\":{\"code\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"invalid or expired key\"}}

support_amy: Sorry about that — we can help. Two quick checks: 1) can you try the same curl from a laptop that bypasses your corp-proxy (to rule out header mangling)? 2) can you paste the raw response headers (redact the key)?

customer-alex: Tried from my laptop (no corp-proxy) and the same curl succeeds. So it looks proxy-related. Raw response headers when calling via service host (through proxy):
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
server: redwood
content-type: application/json
x-request-id: rwd-01GX...
www-authenticate: ApiKey realm=\"redwood\"
```

support_amy: OK that strongly suggests the proxy is altering the Authorization header or wrapping/encoding it. A few things proxies commonly do: base64-encode header values, append characters, or strip colons. Can you check the exact bytes sent by the service? On the service host run:
```
echo -n \"$API_KEY_HEADER_VALUE\" | hexdump -C
# or capture bytes with tcpdump and inspect the HTTP header
```

customer-alex: I don't have tcpdump handy but I dumped the header value from our app logs (we log headers before sending, redacted): it looks like the Authorization value is coming through as `QX...==:extra` (base64-ish with a suffix). We use a corporate HTTP wrapper that vendor installed.

infra_jay: We had a similar support case where the corp proxy's auth-wrapper base64-encoded header values then appended a colon+session token. That will break Redwood's key validation because the service expects the raw API key string. Workarounds: 1) configure the proxy to passthrough the Authorization header unmodified, 2) if proxy supports it, disable header encoding for the destination host, or 3) use an alternate header that the proxy doesn't touch (x-api-key) if your infra allows it.

api_sam: For immediate unblock, try sending the key in the x-api-key header instead of Authorization (many proxies leave custom headers alone):
```
curl -i -H 'x-api-key: sk_live_XXXXREDACTEDXXXX' https://api.redwoodinference.example/v1/generate
```
If that succeeds, we can mark this as header-mangling and provide long-term recommendations.

customer-alex: Tried x-api-key via the same service host — success, requests now return 200 and generation works. Switching to x-api-key for now.

support_amy: Great. We'll note this as a proxy-header-mangling case. For long-term fix we recommend working with your proxy vendor to disable Authorization header encoding for calls to api.redwoodinference.example, or terminate the proxy for that backend. Also consider rotating the key (done already) and verifying there are no trailing whitespace or control chars — those also cause 401s.

support_amy: I'll open an internal ticket to capture details and add a KB entry for proxy header encoding patterns. Ticket: SUP-2026-4821. Tagging @infra_jay and @api_sam.

support-bot: Created ticket SUP-2026-4821 and linked this thread.

customer-alex: Thanks everyone, switching to x-api-key is a good temporary fix. We'll engage our proxy team to update the passthrough rules. :thumbsup:
